answer: A stake-weighted reputation ladder resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable deposit that grows with every verified job, so creating fake identities costs real capital instead of free clicks. Newcomers start on a low-trust terrace where they can only take small tasks, and only consistent, attested work earns them access to higher-value work, the nectar of the economy. A velvet rope of peer review then checks anomalous clusters before payouts, making mass fake accounts unprofitable because the deposit lost exceeds any reward gained.
